summary: Buffalo is the better team on the numbers we have: 32.8 points per game and 6.7153 yards per play this season against Las Vegas at 26.4 and 5.1631, each over five games. But the moneyline on Buffalo is -230 at best, past the -200 line I will not bet, and the Las Vegas side at +200 is priced close to the books' own fair probability of 0.3247, so I pass. The spread sits at BUF -5 after a first capture of -4.5, and the books' de-vigged probabilities are 0.5022 and 0.4978, a coin flip. Nothing in the data shows the number is wrong by a point or more, so I pass. The total has moved up from 51.5 to 54. Both offenses score and both defenses give up plenty, so the price probably already holds that, and I pass. What matters in what we are missing: the importance of any injured player is not measured, Las Vegas lists 3 players out including two skill players, Buffalo has two receivers questionable, and both quarterbacks are projections rather than confirmed starters.

reasons.claim: Buffalo is the stronger side on season numbers, but the best price on them is -230, which is past the -200 limit, so the favourite cannot be taken.
The books' own de-vigged number already makes Buffalo the clear favourite, and nothing in the data says the underdog is worth backing at its price.

calls.what_would_change_it: A Buffalo quarterback change on the injury report would move this, but no price on Buffalo at -200 or worse is ever a bet for me.

reasons.claim: The books' de-vigged probabilities on the two sides are almost identical, so the market sees this number as close to even, and nothing in the data shows it is wrong in points.
Buffalo is the better team on form, yet the number has already moved toward Buffalo from where it was first captured, so the price holds some of that.
The number sits between the scoring key numbers of 3 and 6, so it is not on one of them, and Las Vegas's last three games rest on a thin window that includes a large loss.

calls.what_would_change_it: A change in the quarterback listed for either side, or the number moving off BUF -5 toward BUF -4.5, would make me look at this again.

reasons.claim: Both teams score and both give up points, and the total has already risen from where it was first captured, so the price probably holds that.
The books' de-vigged probabilities on Under and Over are essentially equal, and the data gives nothing about this market beyond its own price and team averages.

calls.what_would_change_it: A quarterback change or a player ruled out on the injury report could move the total, and that would make me look again.
